subject.title: fix #98107: Gateway regenerates service-env file on every restart, wiping Telegram bot tokens

question: Should OpenClaw preserve generated macOS LaunchAgent env-file SecretRef credential values during regeneration when current config still references the key and installed provenance is file-backed?
rationale: The patch is narrow and improves channel availability, but it deliberately carries a credential forward from an existing generated env file, which is a credential-handling and upgrade-policy choice rather than a purely mechanical code repair.

options.title: Accept bounded preservation
options.body: Merge after required checks if maintainers accept preserving only file-backed or inline-and-file SecretRef values whose keys still appear in current config, with dotenv, shell, exec, and auth sources taking precedence.

options.title: Require exact-head macOS proof
options.body: Ask for a repeat macOS LaunchAgent regeneration proof on the latest head if the previous live proof plus final focused tests are not enough for this credential path.

options.title: Pause for broader secret policy
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers decide whether generated env files may be used as a durable credential fallback at all.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded preservation
recommendation.body: Merge after required checks if maintainers accept preserving only file-backed or inline-and-file SecretRef values whose keys still appear in current config, with dotenv, shell, exec, and auth sources taking precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned and authored the latest commits that narrowed the preservation boundary.
